body:
Sounds like a simple solution, but kind of mismatches the `profiler_path` option name.
I wonder if we should rename the option back to `profiler` (although that might make it harder to figure out how to use tracy/perfetto), or if we should accept `"instruments"` as well as a path the the `Instruments.app`?
I think you can use the existing `_GD_VARNAME_CONCAT_` instead.

Needs to be a path, otherwise this returns false
```suggestion
    if path == pathlib.Path("instruments"):
```

Maybe there should be two options, `profiler` and `profiler_path`, so you can also do better checks/error handling for Tracy and Perfetto (if user passed `profiler=tracy profiler_path=something/not/tracy` you can return an error and tell the user how to set up Tracy for compiling - linking the docs most likely.)

The current system where you somehow need to pass a path to a supported profiler (only discoverable through docs) seems a bit unintuitive. With an explicit `profiler=(tracy|perfetto|instruments)` we could also envision having a system like `d3d12=yes` does to look up the relevant files in `bin`, downloaded via a script in `misc/scripts`.

Those are already included in the header.

(If you find a way to remove some from the header to reduce the impact of that header on compilation time, that would also be good, but from a quick look I don't see anything obvious - and it's `profiling.h` is only included in `.cpp` files so not too bad.)
It seems to be building and running fine without these include.
I have refactored to introduce an `EnumVariable` called `profiler` that allows for `tracy`, `perfetto` or `instruments`, so it is more intuitive.
Please handle the `elif env["profiler_path"]` case (as Remi said, "print a helpful error and return" is probably a good solution).
